whatItIs.heading: What is mold remediation?
whatItIs.body:
Mold remediation is the professional process of containing, removing, and cleaning mold growth from a property and addressing the moisture source that allowed it to establish. It is not the same as mold testing or inspection, which are diagnostic steps. Remediation is the intervention.

The process follows a defined sequence: identify and stop the moisture source, establish containment with plastic barriers and negative air pressure to prevent cross-contamination during removal, remove mold-affected materials that cannot be cleaned in place, HEPA-vacuum and treat remaining surfaces, and verify the result with clearance testing. Mold produces mycotoxins and volatile organic compounds that affect indoor air quality. A successful remediation does not simply hide visible growth—it eliminates the colony at the substrate level and restores the moisture conditions that prevent regrowth.

steps.title: Moisture source identification
steps.body: Gallagher technicians locate the moisture source driving mold growth using thermal imaging cameras and calibrated moisture meters before any remediation begins. Removing mold without eliminating the moisture source guarantees regrowth. The source—whether a plumbing leak, roof intrusion, or HVAC condensate problem—is documented and addressed.

steps.title: Containment and negative air pressure
steps.body: Plastic sheeting and containment barriers isolate the work area. HEPA air scrubbers run under negative pressure, exhausting filtered air outside the structure. This prevents mold spores disturbed during removal from migrating to clean areas of the home.

steps.title: Material removal and HEPA cleaning
steps.body: Mold-affected drywall, insulation, and porous building materials that cannot be cleaned in place are removed, bagged, and disposed of per California regulations. Structural framing and hard surfaces are HEPA-vacuumed, treated with an EPA-registered antimicrobial, and allowed to dry before encapsulation if applicable.

steps.title: Clearance testing and reconstruction
steps.body: An independent third-party clearance test confirms spore counts have returned to acceptable levels before containment comes down. Gallagher coordinates the clearance test and, once cleared, transitions directly to reconstruction—replacing removed drywall, insulation, and finishes without a subcontractor handoff.

signs.heading: Signs you need professional mold remediation
signs.intro: Visible growth is one indicator. Mold often establishes inside wall cavities, beneath flooring, and above ceiling tile long before it surfaces.

items.title: Visible mold growth on any surface
items.body: Any mold colony visible to the naked eye—black, green, gray, or white—warrants professional assessment. The visible portion is typically the smaller part of the growth; the substrate behind it is usually more affected.

items.title: Persistent musty or earthy odor
items.body: A musty smell that does not resolve with ventilation is a reliable indicator of active mold growth, usually inside a wall cavity, beneath a floor, or above a ceiling. The odor is microbial off-gassing from an active colony.

items.title: Past water intrusion that was not professionally dried
items.body: Any area that experienced a plumbing leak, roof leak, or flooding that was not dried with professional equipment within 48 to 72 hours has a high probability of mold colonization, even without visible growth at the surface.

items.title: Health symptoms in occupants
items.body: Persistent respiratory symptoms, allergic reactions, or headaches that improve when occupants leave the home and return when they come back are a documented pattern associated with elevated indoor mold exposure.

items.title: Warped, stained, or soft drywall or flooring
items.body: Drywall that bulges or shows brown staining, and flooring that feels soft underfoot, both indicate moisture behind the surface—conditions that support active mold growth in the substrate.

whyUs.heading: Why homeowners call Gallagher for mold remediation
whyUs.body:
Mold remediation done incorrectly has two predictable outcomes: the mold comes back, or the remediation spreads spores to previously clean areas of the home. Both failures trace to the same root cause—skipping containment, missing the moisture source, or treating visible growth without addressing the substrate behind it.

Gallagher Restoration Co. has performed mold remediation across Southern California for more than 15 years. IICRC-trained technicians establish negative-air containment before any materials are touched, document the moisture source before any materials are removed, and coordinate third-party clearance testing at the close of every job. Remediation is not declared complete until an independent lab confirms spore counts have returned to acceptable levels. When reconstruction is needed after material removal, the same crew handles it—no separate contractor, no scheduling gap. Call (951) 541-0034 to schedule an on-site assessment; there is no charge for the initial visit.

pricing.heading: Mold remediation pricing—what to expect
pricing.body: Every mold remediation job starts with a free on-site assessment. Mold remediation in Southern California typically ranges from $1,500 to $20,000 or more. The lower end covers a single small affected area—a bathroom wall or a cabinet base, for example—where containment is straightforward and material removal is limited. The upper end reflects whole-house contamination requiring full negative-air containment across multiple zones, removal of significant quantities of drywall and insulation, and reconstruction afterward. The moisture source, affected square footage, number of impacted rooms, and whether structural material removal is required all drive the final number. Many mold remediation jobs are covered wholly or partially by homeowners insurance when the underlying moisture source is a covered loss. Gallagher Restoration Co. documents the scope and coordinates with your carrier from the initial visit forward.

faqs.q: What is the difference between mold remediation and mold removal?
faqs.a: The terms are often used interchangeably, but professional remediation is broader than simple removal. Remediation includes identifying and eliminating the moisture source, establishing containment to prevent spore spread during the work, removing affected materials, treating remaining surfaces, and verifying the result with clearance testing. Removal without those steps typically leads to regrowth.

faqs.q: How long does mold remediation take?
faqs.a: Most residential mold remediation projects take two to five days for the remediation phase, plus one to two days for clearance test results before containment comes down. Projects requiring reconstruction add additional time depending on scope. Gallagher Restoration Co. provides a written timeline during the initial on-site assessment.

faqs.q: Does homeowners insurance cover mold remediation in California?
faqs.a: Coverage depends on the cause. Mold resulting from a sudden and accidental covered water loss—a burst pipe, appliance failure, or storm-driven roof leak—is typically covered. Mold from long-term gradual leakage or deferred maintenance is generally excluded. Gallagher Restoration Co. documents the moisture source and cause from the initial visit to support the insurance claim.

faqs.q: Can I stay in my home during mold remediation?
faqs.a: It depends on the location and extent of the affected area. Small, contained remediation in a bathroom or utility room often allows occupancy in unaffected parts of the home. Whole-house contamination or remediation involving the HVAC system typically requires temporary relocation until clearance testing confirms the space is safe.

faqs.q: Are there health risks associated with water damage and mold?
faqs.a: Yes. Mold and bacteria thrive in moist environments and are linked to respiratory issues, allergic reactions, asthma flare-ups, and general indoor-air quality problems. Sensitive occupants—children, older adults, and anyone with asthma or a compromised immune system—are typically the first to show symptoms. Prompt water dry-out and, when needed, professional mold remediation are the reliable ways to remove the risk.
